preamble: Insertion of [s] where the standard language has none occurs in Dominican Spanish, whose speakers delete or aspirate syllable-final /s/. Speakers restoring the prestige form overshoot and insert [s] before consonants, especially voiceless stops, and after function words. The best-known case is the joking register called hablar fisno 'speaking finely', but Bullock and Toribio (2009) also record s-insertion among rural children of El Cibao with little exposure to the standard.

examples.note: Source of the register name hablar fisno 'speaking finely'.
Hypercorrection of the vernacular jagual / jaguai. The from forms are the standard pronunciation, which has no [s].
Word-final /s/ is dropped while [s] is inserted before the coda stops /d/ and /b/.

sources: Bullock, B. E. & Toribio, A. J. (2009). Reconsidering Dominican Spanish: Data from the rural Cibao. Revista Internacional de Lingüística Iberoamericana 7(2), 49–73. https://www.jstor.org/stable/41678401
